G04-exp-dedicated-agent.summary: Observed on fixture ca1: a dedicated agent (HOME=<tmp> ssh-agent -U -d -a <tmp>/agent/agent.sock) holding a disposable ed25519 K_env plus certificate (private file deleted after ssh-add -t 120) listed exactly 2 entries (ED25519, ED25519-CERT, both K_env). Fresh login rc 0 with exactly 1 new Accepted line carrying the certificate ID and 1 agent sign request. With IdentityAgent=none rc 255, no Accepted line. ssh -G and ssh -vvv referenced only the temp socket (0 foreign paths, 0 <home>/.ssh references). After the 120 s lifetime: ssh-add -l 'The agent has no identities.' (rc 1), ssh-add -T rc 1, fresh login rc 255, 2 agent 'expiring key' log lines. Exact-PID kill: agent terminated, socket removed. Verdict pass.

G04-exp-cert-expiry.summary: Observed on fixture ca1 (container-host clock offset 0.008-0.015 s): C1a (default ssh-add) and C1b (ssh-add -N) logged in before valid_before, agent-held and from disk (rc 0, Accepted line with ID). C2 refused with 'Certificate invalid: not yet valid', C3 with 'Certificate invalid: expired' (rc 255). Boundary: 153 back-to-back fresh logins, 80 accepted / 73 refused; last acceptance ended 0.029 s before valid_before, first refusal started 0.021 s before it (its authentication completed after it); none accepted starting after valid_before, none refused ending before it; all 73 refusals logged as expired. At valid_before+5 s both agents still listed the expired certificate and all four variants (agent-held/disk x default/-N) were refused as expired (rc 255). After valid_before+300 s the default-added certificate was gone from agent A (plain key kept, 1 'expiring key' line) while the -N certificate remained in agent B; the same certificate offered from disk was then refused as expired, identical to the agent-held case. Verdict pass. NEW authentication only: existing masters keep admitting sessions after expiry (G09-prelim-mux-after-expiry H1/H1b), so certificate validity does not bound live connections.

G04-exp-principal-scope.summary: Observed (system-level trust, ca1 principals file p-host1, ca2 p-host2, one CA): {p-host1} ca1 rc 0 / ca2 rc 255; {p-host2} ca1 rc 255 / ca2 rc 0; {p-host1,p-host2} rc 0 on BOTH hosts (usable on both, not scoped); {cert} (the username) rc 255 on both; rogue-CA certificate rc 255 on both; bare key rc 255 on both. Every refused certificate was evaluated by sshd (Failed line with its ID); the trusted-CA refusals were logged as 'Certificate does not contain an authorized principal'; the rogue-CA refusal logged no reason at VERBOSE. Verdict pass. Per-destination scope came only from the server-side principal map.

G04-exp-account-ca-principals.summary: Observed on fixture enroll (account-owned authorized_keys, preimage = seed sha256 5c4670f1...): before our line, the hm:fx-enroll:enroll certificate rc 255 and our CA's ops certificate rc 255 against the seed's own cert-authority,principals="ops" line (different CA key; certificate evaluated, no principal reason logged). Added cert-authority,principals="hm:fx-enroll:enroll" <fixture CA> by compare-and-swap on the preimage digest, temp file and atomic rename (rc 0; after-add bytes = preimage + 1 line). Then: hm principal rc 0 (Accepted with ID); enroll (username) rc 255 and ops (our CA) rc 255, both logged 'Certificate does not contain an authorized principal'; bare key rc 255; the pre-existing admin key still worked. Removal by marker rc 0; after-remove bytes identical to the preimage, sha256 = seed, owner:mode enroll:600, no temp files left; hm certificate rc 255 afterwards. Verdict pass.

G04-exp-enroll-marker-key.summary: Observed on fixture enroll: the verification config offered only the marker key (identitiesonly yes, no ControlMaster/ControlPath, publickey only, password/kbd off, dedicated agent). Marker-only fresh login before enrollment rc 255. Marker key appended alongside existing entries by CAS + atomic rename (after-add bytes = preimage + marker line). Marker-only fresh login rc 0 with exactly 1 new Accepted line with the marker fingerprint (1 key offered). Existing admin access still worked. A concurrent administrator append landed (rc 0). Removal of the marker line only (rc 0): after-remove bytes = preimage + the concurrent line (9 -> 10 lines), marker absent. Marker-only login afterwards rc 255. Concurrent line removed; seed sha256 restored, enroll:600, no temp files. Verdict pass.

G04-exp-issuer-separation.summary: Observed: the fixture CA was held by an issuer agent (0700 dir containing just its socket) that signed the parent {p-host1,p-host2} and child {p-host1} certificates (rc 0). Read back from the issued certificates: child principals a strict subset, child valid_before 840 s earlier than the parent's. From the worker-only environment: ssh-add -L showed 2 entries (K_env, certificate) and no CA; ssh-keygen -U -s <CA pub> through the worker socket rc 255, no certificate written. Servers: child on ca1 rc 0 before its expiry; child on ca2 rc 255 ('Certificate does not contain an authorized principal'); after child expiry, child on ca1 rc 255 ('Certificate invalid: expired') while the parent still logged in on ca1 and ca2 (rc 0). Scan of worker/child files (4), agent argv/env and worker env: 0 hits of CA material. Verdict pass against the stated (endpoint) criterion. Findings, not part of the criterion: (1) a same-user process given the issuer socket path obtained a certificate (rc 0); (2) the fixture CA private key FILE stayed readable by the same user from the worker-only environment (mode -rw-------, owned by the harness uid) for the whole experiment. So the 'worker path' separation is an environment and agent-endpoint boundary only, not an OS or file-access boundary.

G04-exp-fresh-login-verification.summary: Observed on fixture ca1 with a live ControlMaster (1 Accepted line at master start): the verification command (ControlMaster=no, ControlPath=none, explicit identity/certificate/agent, publickey only, BatchMode) rc 0 with exactly 1 new Accepted line carrying the expected ID and 1 new TCP connection. Negative control through the control socket: rc 0 with 0 new Accepted lines and 0 new connections, so reuse is not verification. Master closed with -O exit (process gone, socket removed). Verdict pass.

G09-prelim-mux-after-expiry.summary: Observed on fixture ca1 (certificate valid_before = master start + 90 s, ControlPersist=10m, no tty). (1) Certificate expiry does not stop admissions: at valid_before+10 s a fresh login was refused (rc 255, 'Certificate invalid: expired'), but a new multiplexed session through the existing master was ADMITTED (rc 0, no new TCP connection, no new Accepted line), and so was a client with PubkeyAuthentication=no (rc 0) (H1, H1b). (2) ssh -O stop: rc 0 ('Stop listening request sent.'); control socket removed; the master kept running (retitled 'ssh: [stopped mux]'); -O check rc 255; a client connecting AFTER the stop with the old ControlPath opened a new TCP connection that sshd refused as expired (rc 255), and one with PubkeyAuthentication=no was not admitted (rc 255) (H2a, H2b, H2b2). This only shows that the stop closes the door to NEW control connections: control connections the master accepted before the stop were still granted sessions and forwards after it (G09-prelim-mux-preconnected-after-stop, verdict fail), so this run does NOT show that -O stop stops admissions. (3) The already-open session S1 continued: 9 heartbeats after stop, last 44 s after it, normal end (rc 0, S1-END) (H2c); with no other control connection open, the master exited within the 0.5 s poll after S1 ended despite ControlPersist=10m (H2d; with an idle pre-accepted control connection the stopped master stays up). (4) -O exit on a second master: master gone, open session S2 terminated (rc 255, 0 heartbeats after exit), socket removed, later client refused (rc 255) (H3); but the remote no-tty shell of S2 (bash pid 815 in the container) was still running 7 s and 20 s after -O exit, with new sleep children (H3b): closing the connection is not remote-process termination. Verdict pass against the H2 criterion, which is scoped to new control connections. Consequence: owned masters must be CLOSED at the deadline (-O exit or exact-PID termination); -O stop is not a verified admission-stopping control (spec 6.6), and neither expiry nor closure ends remote processes.

G09-prelim-mux-preconnected-after-stop.summary: Observed (raw mux protocol v4 client; host OpenSSH_10.3p1; ca1 and bastion fixtures). Every control check held: masters authenticated once; before the stop the raw client opened a session (MUX_S_SESSION_OPENED, exit 0) and each forward type worked on bastion (local MUX_S_OK + target banner through the new listener; remote MUX_S_REMOTE_PORT + listener accepting inside the container; stdio MUX_S_SESSION_OPENED + banner); a fresh login after valid_before was refused as expired; -O stop rc 0, socket removed, -O check rc 255; a new client after the stop rc 255. Then, on control connections accepted BEFORE the stop: ca1 new session at stop+2.039 s (7.5 s after valid_before) MUX_S_SESSION_OPENED, remote command ran as cert, exit 0, 0 new connections, 0 new Accepted lines (H2e refuted); a second connection idle until stop+15.032 s (20.5 s after valid_before) likewise admitted (H2e2 refuted); bastion local forward at stop+2.037 s MUX_S_OK and the target's SSH banner read through the new 127.0.0.1 listener (H2f refuted); remote forward MUX_S_REMOTE_PORT with the remote listener accepting (H2g refuted); stdio forward MUX_S_SESSION_OPENED with the banner (H2h refuted); bastion logged 0 new connections and 0 Accepted lines meanwhile. Verdict FAIL: ssh -O stop does not stop admissions on control connections it had already accepted. Findings: the stopped master with no session stayed running in 12/12 samples over 12 s while an idle pre-accepted connection was open, and exited within 0.25 s once it closed; SIGTERM to the exact master PID closed the remaining pre-accepted connection (later request: broken pipe) and the local forward listener (connection refused) (H3d); -O exit rc 0 terminated the master and a pre-accepted connection could no longer request a session (broken pipe, 1.0 s later) (H3c).

G09-prelim-mux-stop-race.summary: Observed: 50 iterations, each a fresh master (ControlPersist=3 s) racing a client that cannot authenticate (PubkeyAuthentication=no) against ssh -O stop, start delays uniform client 0-60 ms / stop 0-40 ms. -O stop rc 0 in 50/50. 25 clients started after the stop call had returned: 0 admitted (all 25 went to a fresh connection and were refused with publickey denial). 7 clients overlapped the stop call: 1 admitted, 6 refused. 18 clients started before the stop call: all 18 admitted. All 50 masters exited on their own within ControlPersist+5 s. Server Accepted lines = 50 = masters (no client authenticated itself). Verdict pass against the stated criterion (no admission of a client that STARTED after stop returned). This criterion cannot detect admissions on control connections accepted before the listener closed; such admissions occur (G09-prelim-mux-preconnected-after-stop), and the admitted overlapping client is consistent with that. The race does not show that -O stop stops admissions.
